title: Which sign goes between each pair of expressions?
description: Eight pairs of expressions are compared by reasoning about what differs between the two sides. Brackets are opened, multipliers are compared, and signs are decided without working out the full values.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare two expressions by finding what differs between them, and open brackets to see the terms. Watch for students who work out every value instead of reasoning, or who call a pair equal because it looks alike.

video_script.why: The child compares eight pairs of expressions by reasoning about what differs and what each bracket opens into.
video_script.substitution: Find what differs between the two sides, open any bracket, and decide the sign from that difference.
video_script.anchor: Eight pairs of expressions with a box between each pair
video_script.payoff_line: The boxes take equals, greater than, less than, greater than, equals, greater than, equals and greater than.

final_answer.spoken: the boxes take equals, greater than, less than, greater than, equals, greater than, equals and greater than

never_show: the final value of any of the eight expressions
maths_rules: (a) both sides are the same expression, so =
(b) 83 × 42 has two more lots of 83 than 83 × 40, same take away, so >
(c) 17 × 8 takes away more than 17 × 6, so the left is smaller, <
(f) 76 − 53 = 23 is above zero and 53 − 76 = −23 is below zero, so >
(h) 36 is more than 35 and both brackets are 12, so >
video_script.design: The eight pairs stay on the board in two columns. One pair or two are lit at a time, the difference between the sides is marked, and the sign is written in the box.
open_questions: Pair (a) in the book is the same expression on both sides, 49 − 7 + 8 and 49 − 7 + 8, which looks like a misprint; the worklist answer for it is equals, so the script follows that.

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, the first two pairs.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>In the first pair, both sides are the same, so the sign is equals.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>The second pair has eighty three times forty two against eighty three times forty.
<bookmark mark='s14'/>The left side has two more lots of eighty three, so the sign is greater than.

beats.on_screen: (c) both start at 145; 17 × 8 is taken away on the left and 17 × 6 on the right, so <; (d) the left takes away only 35, the right multiplies 23 by 48 − 35, so >

marks.s21: the third pair is shown with both sides starting at 145
marks.s22: the bigger take away on the left is marked and < is written
marks.s23: the whole product 23 × 48 is marked on the left of the fourth pair
marks.s24: the smaller number 48 − 35 is marked on the right and > is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, the third and fourth pairs.
Both sides of the third pair start at one hundred and forty five.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The left takes away seventeen times eight, and the right takes away seventeen times six. The left takes away more, so the sign is less than.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>In the fourth pair, only thirty five is taken away from the whole product on the left.
<bookmark mark='s24'/>On the right, twenty three multiplies a much smaller number, forty eight minus thirty five. The left side is greater.

beats.on_screen: (e) (16 − 11) × 12 = 16 × 12 − 11 × 12, the same terms as the right, so =; (f) 76 − 53 is above zero and 53 − 76 is below zero, the same 88, so >

marks.s31: the bracket on the left of the fifth pair opens into two products
marks.s32: it matches the right side term by term and = is written
marks.s33: the two brackets of the sixth pair are placed on a number line
marks.s34: the sign greater than is written in the sixth box

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, the fifth and sixth pairs.
In the fifth pair, open the bracket on the left. It gives sixteen times twelve minus eleven times twelve.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>The right side has the same terms in a new order, so the sign is equals.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>In the sixth pair, seventy six minus fifty three is above zero.
Fifty three minus seventy six is below zero.
<bookmark mark='s34'/>Both are multiplied by eighty eight, so the left is greater.

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, the last two pairs.
In the seventh pair, both brackets add to fifty eight.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>The same twenty five multiplies both, so the sign is equals.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>In the last pair, both brackets work out to twelve.
<bookmark mark='s44'/>Thirty six is more than thirty five, so the left side is greater.

marks.s52: the third pair is tried with small numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='s51'/>Step five, check two pairs with small numbers.
Two times five minus three is seven.
Two times open bracket five minus three close bracket is four.
<bookmark mark='s53'/>Seven is greater than four, which fits the fourth pair.
<bookmark mark='s52'/>Ten minus two times four is two, and ten minus two times three is four.
Two is less than four, which fits the third pair.
